title: Creator platform policy, creator economy, marketing and security sources
description: Official YouTube, Meta and TikTok policy sources that decide whether faceless and AI-assisted channels can monetise, creator-economy publications, search-marketing news and defensive security feeds.

items.title: YouTube channel monetization policies (inauthentic and reused content)
items.summary: Official YouTube Partner Program policy. On 15 July 2025 'repetitious content' was renamed 'inauthentic content' and clarified to cover mass-produced or repetitive uploads; it applies channel-wide and regardless of whether AI was used. Reused-content rules (clips, compilations, reactions) were unchanged.
items.licence: YouTube Help content
items.notes: Official page returned in search results; summary combines the page and coverage quoting it. Re-read before each new series format.
cautions: A faceless series must differ visibly from video to video (topic, script, visuals); near-identical narrated slideshows can cost monetisation for the whole channel.

items.title: YouTube: disclosing use of altered or synthetic content
items.summary: Official help page: creators must disclose realistic altered or synthetic content (a real person saying something they did not, altered real events, realistic invented scenes). Clearly unrealistic, animated or effects content and production assistance are exempt.
items.licence: YouTube Help content
items.notes: Official page returned in search results; introduced March 2024. A May 2026 labelling update was mentioned by a third party but not confirmed.
cautions: Repeated non-disclosure can lead to removal or YouTube Partner Program suspension.

items.licence: YouTube blog content

items.title: Meta for Creators: combating unoriginal content on Facebook
items.summary: Meta's 14 July 2025 announcement: accounts that repeatedly repost others' videos, photos or text without credit or meaningful changes lose monetisation access for a period and get reduced distribution; reshares with commentary or a unique take remain welcome.
items.licence: Meta content
items.notes: Post URL appeared in search results; details come from press coverage quoting it (Tubefilter, Medianama).
cautions: Applies to Facebook monetisation; credit and transform any third-party material, or better, use only your own and licensed media.

items.title: Tubefilter: the fight against unoriginal content is coming to Facebook

items.title: Social Media Today: TikTok launches labels for AI-generated content
items.summary: Coverage of TikTok's AI-generated content label (launched September 2023); TikTok's guidelines require labelling realistic AI depictions of people or scenes and it auto-labels some content via C2PA Content Credentials.
items.licence: Publisher terms
items.notes: TikTok's own support article was not found in search results; check TikTok's Support Center for the current rule.
